Marissa/Ben/David —

I just had the Lena ask below. They want a 6-month hold on unit price for a projected +30% usage bump and a one-time onboarding credit. Finance will need a small concession to approve the uplift. I sketched two options (numbers are rounded):

Option A — Conservative (no price hold):
- 12-month renewal, 15% committed discount vs list
- Standard onboarding credit: $10k one-time credit
- Capacity uplift priced at published rates (overage billed monthly)

Option B — Aggressive (temporary hold & incentive):
- 12-month renewal with a 6-month price hold at current effective rate (their current blended rate)
- 18% committed discount thereafter for remaining term
- One-time onboarding credit: $25k
- Conditional: if usage > 35% above baseline in first 3 months, automatic step-up to dedicated burst pool (ops approval required)

Tradeoffs: Option B materially reduces short-term revenue but increases likelihood of expansion and accelerates commit. Lena said procurement needs a final termsheet by next Tue (2027-06-22).

Approval needed: Can we approve Option B up to $25k credit + 6-month hold? If not, what's the maximum credit we can grant without VP sign-off?

Thanks —
Grace

Grace — quick take from revenue ops: Option B is okay if we protect against downside with a usage-based true-up and a hard cap on the credit drawdown. My recommended guardrails: 
- $25k onboarding credit max (payable as invoice credit on first renewal invoice)
- 6-month price hold limited to baseline + 30% uplift (i.e., new usage within that buffer honored at hold rate)
- If their usage exceeds the 30% buffer in months 1-3, remove price hold for remainder of term and trigger instant partial true-up (pro-rated).

If legal is comfortable with the conditional language, I can present Option B with those guardrails. No VP sign-off needed if credit <= $25k and we include the true-up language.
